mainTopic: Combining witnesses who do not fully match, keeping judges' votes secret, and when late evidence can overturn a verdict
overview: The amud first settles a contradiction: רב חסדא and רב יהודה are two different people who may simply disagree. The נהרדעי then rule that witnesses who differ on a small detail, like the color of the coins, still combine. The גמרא finds their source in בית הלל, who say 100 is included in 200. Cases of wine versus oil and upper versus lower floor are also accepted. Next comes the rule that a judge may not reveal how the judges voted, with a story of a student sent out for revealing secrets. A new משנה follows about late evidence. It asks whether new proof can overturn a verdict after a thirty-day deadline, or after someone said 'I have no witnesses.' רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argues for the litigant. The גמרא rules like him in the first case and like the חכמים in the second, and explains what each double ruling adds. Stories about רב נחמן close the amud: a child who did not know his father's affairs, and a woman holding a שטר she says was paid. רבא's challenge in the second version of that story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two different rabbis may simply disagree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers an earlier contradiction by saying you cannot set one rabbi's statement against another rabbi's statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are you comparing one man against another man?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from just before: why do רב חסדא and רב יהודה seem to contradict each other? It says there is no problem, because each one is a different person with his own view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A contradiction is only a problem when the same person seems to say two opposite things. Here רב חסדא holds that a mismatch in minor details does not cancel testimony, even in capital cases, and רב יהודה holds that it does. They simply disagree, and neither has to follow the other.

keyTerms.meaning: You are throwing (one against the other), meaning you are pointing out a contradiction

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a ruling on the topic. The גמרא is only explaining why two rabbis' opinions do not have to agree with each other.

phrases.english: Are you setting one man against another man?
phrases.notes: The two men are רב חסדא and רב יהודה from just before. Each is allowed to hold his own opinion.

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּבְרָא אַגַּבְרָא קָא רָמֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a contradiction raised just before this section, between רב חסדא and רב יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Disputing parties: the two statements belong to different אמוראים who disagree.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The questioner thought the two statements should agree, so the mismatch looked like a problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is no difficulty, because רב חסדא and רב יהודה hold different opinions.

steps.title: Black coin versus white coin still combines
steps.stepSummary: The נהרדעי rule that two witnesses who disagree on the color of the coin still combine to make valid testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rabbis of נהרדעא say: even if one witness says it was a black מנה and the other says it was a white מנה, their testimonies combine.
steps.whatsHappening: A new opinion is introduced. The rabbis of נהרדעא say that a mismatch about what the coins looked like does not stop the two witnesses from counting together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both witnesses agree on the main point: a מנה is owed. They disagree only about a detail, the coin's color. The נהרדעי say that detail does not matter, which is a lenient position, since the witnesses do seem to contradict each other here.

keyTerms.meaning: The rabbis of the city of נהרדעא
A sum of one hundred דינרים
They combine; the two witnesses count together as a valid pair

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the main question of the section: can witnesses who directly contradict each other on a detail still be joined together?

phrases.english: The rabbis of Neharde'a say:
Even if one says "a black maneh,"
phrases.notes: Black probably means old, darkened coins. White means shiny, new ones.

phrases.english: and one says "a white maneh," they combine.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְהַרְדָּעֵי אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the contradiction in step 1 was resolved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses who disagree about the color of the coins still combine as valid testimony for the debt.

steps.title: Whose opinion do the נהרדעי follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which earlier authority the נהרדעי are following and suggests רבי יהושע בן קרחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this? Is it like רבי יהושע בן קרחה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks for an earlier source for the נהרדעי's ruling. Its first guess is רבי יהושע בן קרחה, who also allows combining witnesses whose testimonies are not identical.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן קרחה is known for letting two separate testimonies combine. The גמרא suggests the נהרדעי might be building on him. This guess is a setup, and the very next step tests whether it really fits.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? Whose opinion does this follow?
A תנא who allows combining separate testimonies

phrases.english: In accordance with whom? In accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן? כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the source behind the ruling of the נהרדעי in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which earlier תנא supports the lenient ruling of the נהרדעי?

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן קרחה is not a fit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion, because רבי יהושע בן קרחה only spoke about witnesses who do not contradict each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe you heard רבי יהושע בן קרחה say this where the witnesses do not contradict each other. But where they do contradict each other, did he say it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own guess. It points out an important difference between רבי יהושע בן קרחה's case and the case of the נהרדעי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יהושע בן קרחה's case, the two witnesses each add something different, but neither says the other is wrong. In the black and white coin case, the witnesses clash directly: the coin cannot be both black and white. So proof from a case with no clash cannot support a case that has one.

keyTerms.meaning: Say that you heard him (only in this case)
Did he say? (meaning: he did not say that)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse two kinds of mismatch. Adding different details is not the same as directly contradicting each other. That difference is the whole point of this step.

phrases.aramaic: אֵימַר דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה
phrases.english: Say that you heard Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha say this
where they do not contradict each other;
where they do contradict each other, did he say it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the source suggested in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי יהושע בן קרחה as the source for the ruling of the נהרדעי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His case has no direct contradiction between the witnesses, while the black and white coin case does.

steps.title: The real source: 100 is included in 200
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the נהרדעי follow a ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. In it, both בית שמאי and בית הלל agree that if one group says 200 and the other says 100, the testimony stands for 100.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the נהרדעי follow this תנא. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said, בית שמאי and בית הלל did not disagree about two groups of witnesses where one says 200 and one says 100, because 100 is included in 200.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a better source for the נהרדעי. It is a ברייתא about two groups of witnesses who give different amounts, and the ברייתא continues in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two groups do clash: one says 200 and the other says 100. Even so, everyone agrees the testimony holds for 100, because the bigger amount includes the smaller one. This shows a תנא who accepts testimony despite a real mismatch, which is closer to the black and white coin case. The ברייתא goes on to describe the case where בית שמאי and בית הלל do argue.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא whose ברייתא is quoted here
One hundred is included within two hundred

steps.whatToRemember: The נהרדעי's leniency does not come from רבי יהושע בן קרחה, whose witnesses never clash. It comes from רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, whose ברייתא accepts testimony even when the witnesses give different amounts.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that a larger amount includes a smaller one is a basic tool for saving testimony when witnesses disagree about amounts.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הוּא דְּאָמַר כִּי הַאי תַּנָּא,
phrases.english: Rather, they said it in accordance with this tanna,
phrases.notes: They means the נהרדעי from step 2.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: as it is taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree
about two sets of witnesses,
where one says two hundred
and one says a maneh,
because a maneh is included within two hundred.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הוּא דְּאָמַר כִּי הַאי תַּנָּא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the source rejected in step 4 with a better one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The נהרדעי follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's ברייתא, which accepts testimony even when the witnesses differ on the amount.

steps.title: Where בית שמאי and בית הלל disagree: one set of witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that the argument is about one set of two witnesses. בית שמאי say their testimony is split and fails. בית הלל say 100 is included in 200.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do they disagree? About one set of witnesses. בית שמאי say their testimony is divided. בית הלל say 100 is included in 200.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the ברייתא from the last step. It shows where בית שמאי and בית הלל argue: when the two witnesses of a single pair contradict each other on the amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said both sides agree when there are two separate groups of witnesses. Here we learn they argue when the two witnesses are one pair, one saying 200 and the other 100. בית הלל let the testimony stand for 100 even though the witnesses contradict each other, and that is the source for the נהרדעי.

keyTerms.meaning: One set: a single pair of witnesses
Their testimony is divided, so it does not count
The two great schools of תנאים

steps.whatToRemember: According to בית הלל, a single pair of witnesses who contradict each other still counts for the smaller amount that both of their statements include. This is the source the נהרדעי rely on.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. With two separate groups of witnesses, everyone agrees the testimony counts for 100. The argument is only about one pair, where each witness says a different amount.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?
About one set of witnesses,
phrases.notes: One witness says 200 and his partner says 100.

phrases.english: for בית שמאי say:
Their testimony is divided,
and בית הלל say:
A maneh is included within two hundred.
phrases.notes: A מנה is 100 דינרים.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל מָה נֶחְלְקוּ? עַל כַּת אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted in step 5 and supplies the actual support for the נהרדעי.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling of the נהרדעי that contradicting witnesses still combine
steps.raayaSupportSource: בית הלל in the ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: one pair saying 200 and 100 counts for 100

steps.title: A real case of wine versus oil before רבי אמי
steps.stepSummary: One witness said a barrel of wine and the other said a barrel of oil. רבי אמי made the defendant pay a barrel of wine, since that amount is included in a barrel of oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: One witness says a barrel of wine, and the other says a barrel of oil. This really happened and came before רבי אמי. He required the defendant to pay a barrel of wine out of the barrel of oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real court case in which the witnesses disagreed about what was in the barrel. רבי אמי ordered payment of the smaller amount, a barrel of wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine was cheaper than oil. So רבי אמי treated the wine as included in the oil, the way 100 is included in 200. The defendant pays only the amount both witnesses agree on.

phrases.english: One says: “A barrel of wine,”
and one says: “A barrel of oil.”
There was such an incident,
and it came before רבי אמי.
רבי אמי obligated him to pay him
a barrel of wine
out of a barrel of oil.
phrases.notes: Wine was cheaper, so its value fits inside the value of the oil. That smaller amount is what both witnesses agree on.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה עוֹבָדָא, וְאָתֵי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a practical ruling that resembles the 100 and 200 principle, but with different items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When witnesses disagree between wine and oil, the defendant pays the value of the cheaper item, wine.

steps.title: Does רבי אמי follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion רבי אמי's ruling follows and suggests רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom? According to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which earlier authority stands behind רבי אמי's ruling. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The obvious candidate is the ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, where 100 is included in 200. The question mark hints that the match may not be perfect.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? Whose opinion is this?

phrases.english: According to whom?
According to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן? כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the source of רבי אמי's ruling, the same way step 3 looked for the source of the נהרדעי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which earlier authority רבי אמי's ruling is based on

steps.title: Wine and oil are not like 100 and 200
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר spoke only where 100 is part of 200. Would he say the same about two completely different items?
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said this where 100 is included in 200. Did he say it in a case like this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion. Wine and oil are two different things, so one is not part of the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 200 and 100, both witnesses could be right: one saw part of the loan and the other saw all of it. With wine and oil, the witnesses truly contradict each other about what the item was. So רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's case may not stretch to cover this one.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he say? (expecting the answer no)

phrases.aramaic: אֵימַר דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
phrases.english: Granted that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said it
where a maneh is included within two hundred,
in a case like this, did he say it?
phrases.notes: Wine is not a smaller part of oil. They are simply different things.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggestion of step 8 by pointing out how the cases differ.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proposed link between רבי אמי's ruling and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר dealt with a smaller amount inside a larger one, not with two different items.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion in step 8 that רבי אמי's wine-and-oil ruling follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר only spoke where a smaller amount is included in a larger one. Wine and oil are different items, so neither testimony includes the other.

steps.title: The case was about money value
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אמי's case was about the value of the barrels. That makes it just like 100 inside 200.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for the value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection. The witnesses were testifying about the money value of a barrel of wine or a barrel of oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the witnesses were only arguing about an amount of money, the smaller sum, the wine's value, is contained in the larger sum, the oil's value. So the case fits רבי שמעון בן אלעזר after all, and רבי אמי's ruling follows him.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for this case; this ruling applies only where...

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אמי's ruling follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר because the witnesses were testifying about money value. A smaller sum is always included in a larger sum.

phrases.english: No, it is needed only
for the value.
phrases.notes: One witness says he owes the value of a barrel of wine, and the other says the value of a barrel of oil.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, לִדְמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the objection of step 9 by redefining the case of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא): the testimony was about money value, not the items themselves
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The witnesses disagreed about two different items, so neither statement includes the other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The witnesses disagreed about money amounts, and the cheaper amount is included in the more expensive one, just like 100 in 200.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אמי's ruling fits רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: the cheaper value is included in the more expensive value.

steps.title: Witnesses disagree about upper or lower floor
steps.stepSummary: One witness says the event happened on the upper floor and the other says the lower floor. רבי חנינא reports that רבי combined their testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: One witness says, 'It was on the upper floor,' and the other says, 'It was on the lower floor.' רבי חנינא said: A case like this came before רבי, and he combined their testimony.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more case of two witnesses who do not match exactly. רבי still counted them together as one valid set of witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witnesses agree on the main event and disagree only on a side detail, which floor it happened on. רבי treated that difference as unimportant and joined their testimony. This follows the same idea as the previous steps: when the core of the testimony matches, a small difference does not cancel it.

keyTerms.meaning: A story or floor of a building
An actual case came before (a רבי)

steps.whatToRemember: A difference in a side detail, like which floor, does not cancel testimony when the witnesses agree on the main event.

phrases.english: One says: "On the upper floor,"
and one says: "On the lower floor."
Rabbi Chanina said:
An incident came before Rabbi,
phrases.notes: Plain "רבי" means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: and he combined their testimony.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מַעֲשֶׂה בָּא לִפְנֵי רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds one more case where witnesses differ only on a side detail, closing the topic of combining testimony.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses who disagree only about which floor the event happened on are combined into one testimony.

steps.title: Source that a judge may not reveal how the judges voted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule and brings a ברייתא with two פסוקים showing that a judge may not say 'I voted to acquit, but I was outvoted.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And from where do we know that when he leaves, and so on.' The Rabbis taught: From where do we know that when a judge leaves court he should not say, 'I said he was innocent and my colleagues said he was liable, but what can I do, they outnumbered me'? The פסוק says, 'Do not go as a talebearer among your people,' and it also says, 'One who goes as a talebearer reveals a secret.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and brings a ברייתא that gives its source in the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A judge who tells the litigant how each judge voted is acting as a רכיל, a talebearer. The second פסוק adds that a talebearer reveals secrets, so the court's discussion counts as a secret that must stay private.

keyTerms.meaning: Talebearer, someone who spreads private information

phrases.english: "And from where do we know that when he leaves," etc.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the opening words of this line in the משנה; כו׳ means "and so on."

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
From where do we know that when he leaves, he should not say:
"I found him innocent and my colleagues found him liable,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מָה אֶעֱשֶׂה שֶׁחֲבֵירַי רַבּוּ עָלַי?
phrases.english: but what can I do, since my colleagues outnumbered me?"
The verse says: "Do not go as a talebearer among your people,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:16

phrases.english: and it says: "One who goes as a talebearer reveals a secret."
phrases.notes: משלי 11:13

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן, מִנַּיִין לִכְשֶׁיֵּצֵא לֹא יֹאמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of witnesses to the next rule in the משנה, about judges keeping their votes secret.
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's rule that a judge may not reveal that he was outvoted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 19:16 (not to be a רכיל) and משלי 11:13 (a רכיל reveals secrets).

steps.title: Student removed for revealing a secret years later
steps.stepSummary: A rumor came out that a student had revealed something said in the בית מדרש 22 years earlier, and רב אמי removed him from the בית מדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain student about whom a rumor went out that he had revealed something said in the בית מדרש, after twenty-two years. רב אמי removed him from the בית מדרש. He said: 'This one reveals secrets.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing how seriously the Rabbis treated revealing private matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though 22 years had passed, רב אמי still sent the student out of the בית מדרש. His reason was that a person who reveals secrets cannot be trusted. This backs up the previous step: private discussions must stay private.

keyTerms.meaning: A rumor went out about him

steps.whatToRemember: Revealing private discussions is serious, and it is not excused even many years later.

phrases.english: There was a certain student
about whom a rumor went out
that he revealed a matter
that was said in the study hall
after twenty-two years.
Rav Ami removed him from the study hall.
He said: "This one reveals secrets."

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא תַּלְמִידָא דִּנְפַק עֲלֵיהּ קָלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life story that reinforces the rule against revealing secrets.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who reveals what was said privately in the בית מדרש may be removed, even years later, because he cannot be trusted.

steps.title: New proof can overturn a verdict, unless a deadline passed
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: whenever a litigant brings new proof, he can overturn the verdict. If he was given thirty days to bring proof, he can overturn only within those thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Any time a person brings proof, he can overturn the verdict. If he was told, 'Bring all the proofs you have from now until thirty days,' then if he found proof within thirty days he can overturn the verdict, but after thirty days he cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new משנה about bringing new evidence after the court has already ruled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic rule is that a verdict is never fully closed, and new proof can reopen it. But if a deadline of thirty days was set, proof found after that time can no longer overturn the ruling.
steps.confusionAlert: Without a deadline, new proof can overturn the verdict at any time. The thirty-day limit applies only when that deadline was set.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Any time he brings proof,
he overturns the verdict.
If he said to him:
"All the proofs that you have,
bring them from now until thirty days,"
if he found proof within thirty days, he overturns the verdict;
after thirty days, he does not overturn it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁמֵּבִיא רְאָיָה סוֹתֵר אֶת הַדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new topic: reopening a case with new evidence.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: New proof can overturn a verdict at any time, unless a thirty-day deadline was set and has passed.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argues about the thirty-day limit
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees with the thirty-day limit. He asks what a litigant should do if he truly could not find his proof until after the thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said: What is this person supposed to do if he did not find his proof within the thirty days but found it after the thirty days?
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argues against the rule we just learned, that proof brought after thirty days cannot overturn the verdict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא said the thirty-day deadline is final. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל answers with a question: it is not this person's fault that he only found his proof late. So he holds that the litigant can still overturn the verdict even after thirty days.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who here disagrees with the main opinion of the משנה
'What should this one do?' A way of saying he could not have done any better
Thirty, meaning the thirty days the court gave him to bring proof

steps.confusionAlert: Even though this is phrased as a question, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is not asking for information. He is making an argument: the person is not to blame, so he may still overturn the verdict.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
What should this one do,
who did not find [his proof] within thirty [days],
phrases.notes: 'Days' isn't written, but it means the thirty days the court gave him in step 14.

phrases.english: but found it after thirty [days]?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: מָה יַעֲשֶׂה זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreeing opinion on the thirty-day limit from step 14
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proof found after the thirty-day deadline can still overturn the verdict, because the litigant could not have done anything more.

steps.title: Someone who said 'I have no witnesses' and later brings them
steps.stepSummary: If a litigant was asked for witnesses or proof and said he had none, and later produces them, they are worth nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: One side told him: 'Bring witnesses,' and he answered: 'I have no witnesses.' He told him: 'Bring proof,' and he answered: 'I have no proof.' Later he brought proof or found witnesses. This is worth nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case. A litigant said outright that he had no witnesses and no proof, and later he produces them. The ruling is that they count for nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference from step 14 is that here the person himself said he had no evidence. Because of that, evidence that appears later looks made-up, so the תנא קמא does not accept it.

keyTerms.meaning: Proof, such as a document or other evidence
It is worth nothing; it does not count

phrases.english: He said to him: 'Bring witnesses,'
and he said: 'I have no witnesses.'
He said: 'Bring proof,'
and he said: 'I have no proof.'
And after some time he brought proof
or found witnesses —
this is worth nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: ״הָבֵא עֵדִים״, וְאָמַר: ״אֵין לִי עֵדִים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case in the same משנה about late evidence
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses or proof produced after the litigant said he had none are rejected.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: he did not know he had witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees again. Maybe the person honestly did not know he had witnesses or proof when he said he had none.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said: What is this person supposed to do if he did not know he had witnesses and then found witnesses, or did not know he had proof and then found proof?
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argues against the ruling in step 16 with the same kind of question he used in step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא saw 'I have no witnesses' as a statement that blocks any later evidence. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל reads it as an honest statement of what he knew at that moment. Since he truly did not know about the evidence, he may still bring it and overturn the verdict.
steps.whyThisMatters: In both disagreements רבן שמעון בן גמליאל follows one idea: a litigant who acted honestly should not lose his case because of when he happened to find his evidence.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
What should this one do,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ עֵדִים,
phrases.english: who did not know that he had witnesses,
and then found witnesses?

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ רְאָיָה,
phrases.english: [Or one who] did not know that he had proof,
and then found proof?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: מָה יַעֲשֶׂה זֶה שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreeing opinion on the case in step 16
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who honestly did not know about his witnesses or proof may still bring them later.

steps.title: Suddenly producing witnesses or proof when about to lose
steps.stepSummary: If a litigant sees he is about to lose and suddenly calls witnesses, or pulls a proof out from his belt, it is worth nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He saw that he was about to lose the case and said: 'Bring over so-and-so and so-and-so, and they will testify for me,' or he pulled a proof out from under his belt. This is worth nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a case that is clearly suspicious. Someone held back his evidence and brings it out only when he sees he is losing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the evidence was available all along, since the witnesses are named and the document was in his belt. Hiding it until the last moment suggests it is not real. That is different from not knowing about it or not finding it, which were רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reasons in steps 15 and 17.

keyTerms.meaning: Being found liable in the judgment, meaning losing the case
His belt, or a money-pouch worn on the belt

steps.whatToRemember: There are three kinds of late evidence. First, evidence found after the thirty days: the תנא קמא says no, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says yes. Second, evidence brought after saying 'I have none': the תנא קמא says no, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says yes if he truly did not know. Third, evidence hidden and pulled out only when losing: it is worth nothing.

phrases.english: He saw that he was about to be found liable in the judgment,
and said: 'Bring over so-and-so and so-and-so, and they will testify for me,'
or he pulled out a proof from under his belt —
this is worth nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָאָה שֶׁמִּתְחַיֵּיב בַּדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A final case that contrasts with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reasoning in step 17. Here the evidence was clearly available all along and was held back.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Evidence that was held back and brought out only once the litigant sees he is losing is worth nothing.

steps.title: On the thirty-day case, the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the thirty-day case, and adds that the הלכה is not like the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבה בר רב הונא said: The הלכה is like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. And רבה בר רב הונא also said: The הלכה is not like the words of the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by deciding the הלכה in the first argument of the משנה. That is the case of a litigant who finds proof after his thirty days are over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר רב הונא makes two statements. The first is a positive one: follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, so late proof can still overturn the verdict. The second is a negative one: do not follow the חכמים. Saying both looks repetitive, and the next step will ask about exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that comes after the משנה
The practical law follows the opinion of...
The practical law does not follow the opinion of...
The Sages (the anonymous majority view in the משנה)

phrases.english: GEMARA
Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
The halakha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.
phrases.notes: This is about the thirty-day case. Even after thirty days, real new proof can still overturn the verdict.

phrases.english: And Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
The halakha does not follow the words of the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא by deciding the הלכה in the first argument of the משנה (Steps 14-15).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the thirty-day case the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and not the חכמים.

steps.title: Why say both statements? It is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the second statement was needed, since ruling like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל already means not ruling like the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It's obvious! Since he said the הלכה is like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, we already know on our own that the הלכה is not like the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה בר רב הונא for saying the same thing twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are only two sides in this argument. Once you rule for one side, you have automatically ruled against the other. So the second statement seems to add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: It's obvious! (a challenge that a statement is unnecessary)

phrases.english: It's obvious!
Since he said
the halakha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
on our own we know
that the halakha does not follow the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא! כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the double wording of Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second statement of רבה בר רב הונא, that the הלכה is not like the חכמים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ruling for one side of a two-sided argument already means ruling against the other side, so the second statement is extra.

steps.title: The second statement teaches that a ruling like the חכמים is reversed
steps.stepSummary: Without the second statement, we might think following the חכמים is acceptable after the fact. It teaches that such a ruling is reversed.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: that applies only from the start, but after the fact, if a court already ruled like the חכמים, it is fine. So he teaches us that if a court did rule that way, we reverse it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that the second statement adds a real new law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "הלכה כרבן שמעון בן גמליאל" by itself could mean only: do it his way from the start (לכתחילה). It would still leave room to accept, after the fact (דיעבד), a court that followed the חכמים. The words "אין הלכה כחכמים" close that door: such a ruling is not valid and must be undone.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
From the start, the ideal way to act
After the fact, once it was already done
We send it back, we reverse it

steps.confusionAlert: A ruling like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל could have meant only "do it this way from the start." The added negative statement is what makes the opposite ruling actually invalid.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a useful pattern. When a ruling is said both positively and negatively, the negative side can teach that the opposite ruling is reversed even after the fact.

phrases.english: You might have said:
these words apply only from the start,
but after the fact, it is fine,
phrases.notes: He means that if a court already ruled like the חכמים, we might think we leave that ruling alone.

phrases.english: so he teaches us
that if he did act that way, we send it back.
phrases.notes: "Send it back" means the case goes back to court and that ruling is undone.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: הָנֵי מִילֵּי לְכַתְּחִילָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the extra statement teaches a new law about the after-the-fact case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Ruling like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is only the ideal (לכתחילה); a court that followed the חכמים would still stand after the fact.
steps.terutzMaskana: A ruling made like the חכמים is reversed even after the fact.

steps.title: On the case of saying he had no witnesses, the הלכה follows the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: On the case of someone who said he had no witnesses, רבי יוחנן rules like the חכמים and not like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "He said to him: Bring witnesses…" and "רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said…". רבה בר רב הונא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The הלכה is like the חכמים. And רבה בר רב הונא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The הלכה is not like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second argument in the משנה and decides its הלכה. This time the ruling goes against רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person said he had no witnesses and later brings some, they are not accepted, as the חכמים said. Again there is a positive statement and a negative statement, and the next step asks why both are needed. This time the answer is different from Step 21: Step 24 explains that the extra words mark this case as the one exception to following רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for וְכוּלֵּיהּ, "and so on" (the rest of the quote)
The master in whose name רבה בר רב הונא reports this ruling

steps.whatToRemember: Thirty-day case: the הלכה is like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, so late proof that was truly not found earlier is accepted, and a court that rules the other way is reversed. Case of saying "I have no witnesses": the הלכה is like the חכמים, so witnesses brought later are not accepted.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume רבן שמעון בן גמליאל wins both arguments. He wins the first one, but loses the second one.

phrases.english: "He said to him: Bring witnesses, etc."
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה case from Steps 16-17. The person said he had no witnesses and then later found some.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: "Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said, etc."

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halakha follows the words of the Rabbis.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabba bar Rav Huna said that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.
phrases.english: The halakha does not follow Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: הָבֵא עֵדִים כּוּ׳, אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל כּוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first argument of the משנה to the second, using the same positive-and-negative style of ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the case of someone who said he had no witnesses, the הלכה follows the חכמים: witnesses brought later are not accepted.

steps.title: Why add the second half of the ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן said both 'like the חכמים' and 'not like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.' The second half seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it obvious? Once he said the הלכה is like the חכמים, we already know by ourselves that the הלכה is not like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling from step 22 for saying something extra that seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are only two opinions in this argument, so following one side already means rejecting the other. Saying both looks like repeating yourself, and the גמרא assumes every word must teach something.

keyTerms.meaning: It's obvious! (a challenge that something did not need to be said)

phrases.english: It's obvious!
Since he said the halacha is like the words of the Sages,
we know by ourselves

phrases.aramaic: דְּאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.
phrases.english: that the halacha is not like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the extra wording in the ruling from step 22, the same way step 20 questioned the ruling in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The added words 'and not like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל' in step 22.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In a two-sided argument, ruling for one side already rejects the other, so the extra words seem unnecessary.

steps.title: Only this case is an exception
steps.stepSummary: The extra words teach that only in this case is the הלכה not like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. In all his other rulings, the הלכה does follow him.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us that in that case, the הלכה is not like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. This implies that in all the others, the הלכה is like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the extra words narrow the exception to this one case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'in this case not like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל' implies 'but in other cases, yes.' So the extra words set a general rule: wherever רבן שמעון בן גמליאל appears in the משנה, the הלכה follows him, except here.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us
In all of them (all the other cases)

phrases.english: This teaches us
that in that case the halacha is not
like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel;
which implies that in all the others,
the halacha is like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.
phrases.notes: 'All the others' means every other place in the משנה where רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives a ruling.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the exception: the extra words teach that only this case is an exception.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words 'not like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל' seemed to add nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: They teach that only here do we not follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. Everywhere else in the משנה, the הלכה follows him.
steps.whyThisMatters: It turns a ruling on one case into a general rule about how to decide every argument involving רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the משנה.

steps.title: This rejects the list of three exceptions
steps.stepSummary: This general rule rejects רבה בר בר חנה's report from רבי יוחנן. That report said the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל everywhere except three cases: ערב, צידן, and ראיה אחרונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This excludes what רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: everywhere רבן שמעון בן גמליאל taught in our משנה, the הלכה follows him, except for the guarantor, צידן, and the last proof case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the opinion that its answer is arguing against.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר בר חנה's report counts three exceptions. The ruling we just explained allows only one, the ראיה אחרונה case in our משנה. So according to this ruling, in the ערב and צידן cases the הלכה does follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: The city of צידן, where a case took place
The last proof case: the later argument in our משנה, about proof brought after saying 'I have none'

steps.whatToRemember: Only the 'I have no witnesses' case in our משנה is an exception. Everywhere else in the משנה, the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. That is why the list of three exceptions is rejected.
steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions agree that ראיה אחרונה is an exception. They only disagree about ערב and צידן.

phrases.english: This excludes that
which Rabba bar bar Chana said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁשָּׁנָה רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: Any place that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel taught
in our Mishnah, the halacha is like him,
except for the guarantor and Tzaidan
phrases.notes: These are two other משניות where רבן שמעון בן גמליאל rules: one about a loan guarantor, one about a case in the city of צידן.

phrases.english: and the last proof.
phrases.notes: This is the later argument in our own משנה, about someone who said he had no proof and later found some.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאַפּוֹקֵי מֵהָא דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer of step 24 by naming the opinion it rejects.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows what is new in the answer by naming the opposing opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might follow רבה בר בר חנה's report, which counts three exceptions to following רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only ראיה אחרונה is an exception. The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל even in the ערב and צידן cases.

steps.title: A child with no witnesses and no proof
steps.stepSummary: A child was taken to court before רב נחמן. He said he had no witnesses and no proof, so רב נחמן ruled against him.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain child was taken to court before רב נחמן. They asked him, 'Do you have witnesses?' He said, 'No.' 'Do you have proof?' He said, 'No.' רב נחמן ruled that he was liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that shows the 'I have no witnesses' case in real life. This sets up what comes next in the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The child clearly said he had no witnesses and no proof. That is exactly the case of our משנה. With nothing to support him, רב נחמן ruled for the other side.

phrases.english: There was a certain child who was taken to court
before Rav Nachman.
They said to him: Do you have witnesses?
He said to them: No.
Do you have proof?
He said to them: No.
Rav Nachman ruled him liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא יָנוֹקָא דְּתַבְעוּהּ לְדִינָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rulings about 'I have no witnesses' to a real case where someone said exactly that.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A litigant who says he has no witnesses and no proof loses the case.

steps.title: The crying child finds witnesses
steps.stepSummary: After losing in court, the child walks away crying. Some people hear him and say they know about his father's affairs.
steps.simpleTranslation: The child was walking away and crying. Some people heard him and said to him: We know about your father's affairs.
steps.whatsHappening: The story of the child from step 26 continues. Now witnesses suddenly appear, and this sets up רב נחמן's ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 26 the child said he had no witnesses and no proof, so he lost. Now witnesses exist after all. This creates the exact problem of the משנה: can someone who said 'I have no witnesses' bring witnesses later?

phrases.english: He was walking along and crying.
phrases.notes: This is the child from the last step, who just lost his case before רב נחמן.

phrases.english: Some people heard him,
and they said to him:
We know about your father's affairs.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה קָא בָכֵי וְאָזֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the child begun in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses come forward after the child had already said he had none.

steps.title: Even the רבנן agree for a child
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that in this case even the רבנן agree the new witnesses are accepted, because a child does not know his father's affairs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: In this case even the רבנן agree, because a child does not know about his father's affairs.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן rules that the child may bring the new witnesses. Even the רבנן, who usually reject late witnesses, agree here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן usually reject witnesses brought after someone said 'I have no witnesses.' They worry he is playing a trick. A child really does not know what his father did, so when he said 'I have no witnesses' he was simply mistaken. That was not a trick, so his statement does not block him.

keyTerms.meaning: the Sages (the חכמים of the משנה)

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן's rule against late witnesses only applies to someone who should have known. A child does not know his father's affairs, so even the רבנן accept his witnesses.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the רבנן changed their opinion. Their rule still stands. This case is just outside it, because the child's 'no witnesses' statement came from not knowing.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the reason behind the רבנן's rule. They only reject a claim that could be a trick, not an honest mistake.

phrases.english: רב נחמן said:
In this case, even the רבנן agree,
because a child does not know about his father's affairs.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּהָא אֲפִילּוּ רַבָּנַן מוֹדוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב נחמן's ruling on the new witnesses from step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A child who said he had no witnesses may still bring witnesses later, even according to the רבנן, because he did not know his father's affairs.

steps.title: A woman says the שטר she holds was paid
steps.stepSummary: A שטר was found in a woman's possession. She said it had already been paid, and רב נחמן believed her.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a woman from whose hands a שטר came out. She said: I know that this שטר was already paid. רב נחמן believed her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story about רב נחמן. A woman holding a loan document says the debt was already paid, and רב נחמן believes her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שטר was in her hands, so it was given to her to hold. Usually the lender could collect with this document. Because of her word, רב נחמן does not let the lender collect.

keyTerms.meaning: a document; here a loan document

phrases.english: There was a certain woman
from whose hands a שטר came out,
she said (to him):
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: I know about this שטר that it was paid.
רב נחמן believed her.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא אִיתְּתָא דִּנְפַק שְׁטָרָא מִתּוּתֵי יְדַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story about another ruling of רב נחמן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman holding a שטר is believed when she says it was already paid.

steps.title: Does this follow רבי?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן whether his ruling follows רבי, who holds that a שטר is acquired just by handing it over.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: Whose opinion are you following? Is it רבי's, who says that letters (a שטר) are acquired by handing them over?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב נחמן's ruling. He suggests it only works if we follow רבי's opinion about owning a שטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא thinks the only reason to believe her is that she became the owner of the שטר. Then her word about it would count. That depends on רבי's view that handing over a שטר alone makes someone its owner, without writing a separate document. The challenge is that רב נחמן's ruling would then rest on one particular opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: letters; meaning the debt written in a שטר

phrases.english: רבא said to רב נחמן:
Like whom? Like רבי,
who says that letters are acquired by handing them over.
phrases.notes: Handing her the שטר alone would make her its owner, so she could say it was paid.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן? כְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the basis of the ruling in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling believing the woman in step 29.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Believing her seems to require that she owns the שטר. That only works according to רבי's view that a שטר is acquired by handing it over, so the ruling would depend on one opinion.

steps.title: She could have burned it
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that this case is different. She could have burned the שטר if she wanted, so she is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: Here it is different, because if she wanted, she could have burned it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא. His ruling does not depend on רבי at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שטר was in her hands, so she could have destroyed it and the lender would have lost his proof. Since she had that power, we believe her when she simply says it was paid. This is the familiar logic of מיגו: she is believed about a smaller claim because she could have done something bigger.
steps.whatToRemember: The woman is believed because she had full control over the שטר and could have burned it. Ownership of the שטר is not the reason, so the ruling does not depend on רבי.

phrases.english: He said to him: Here it is different,
because if she had wanted, she could have burned it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָכָא, דְּאִי בָּעֲיָא קְלָתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge in step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the ruling, so it no longer depends on רבי's view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא thought the woman is believed only because she owns the שטר, following רבי.
steps.terutzMaskana: She is believed because she could have burned the שטר, and that works according to everyone.

steps.title: A second version: רב נחמן did not believe her
steps.stepSummary: Some say the story went the other way. רב נחמן did not believe the woman who said the שטר had already been paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רב נחמן did not believe her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the woman's case. In this version רב נחמן did not believe her claim that the שטר was paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (Steps 29-31), רב נחמן believed her because she could have burned the שטר. Here the outcome is flipped: he did not accept her word. This sets up a new exchange between רבא and רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say. This introduces a second version of a story or ruling.
He believed her, or accepted her claim as trustworthy.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new case. It is the same woman and the same שטר from Step 29, told with the opposite outcome.

phrases.english: Some say:
Rav Naḥman did not believe her.
phrases.notes: She is the woman who held the שטר and said it had already been paid (Step 29).

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the Step 29 story, in which רב נחמן reaches the opposite ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, רב נחמן did not accept the woman's claim that the שטר had been paid.

steps.title: רבא starts to argue that she could have destroyed the שטר
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן. He begins to say that if she had wanted to, she could have destroyed the שטר, so she should be believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: But if she had wanted to...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins a challenge to רב נחמן's ruling in this second version. His sentence is cut off here and finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא is using the same reasoning that appears in the first version (Step 31): she could have burned the שטר. If she had that power, why not believe her when she says it was paid? The sentence finishes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely. This word often opens a challenge.

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Naḥman:
But if she had wanted to —
phrases.notes: The sentence finishes on the next amud. He means she could have burned the שטר, like in Step 31.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן וְהָא אִי בָּעֲיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second-version ruling from Step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling (second version) not to believe the woman.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since she could have destroyed the שטר if she wanted to, her claim that it was paid should be believed. This is the same reasoning as Step 31. The argument is completed on the next amud.
